Fig. 1: Pruning a quaternion message passing neural network. Graph's features are first transformed into quaternion features. We train QMPNN, which has quaternion weights, for the given task. Furthermore, to find our proposed winning lottery ticket, we prune and train the QMPNN until we get a model with pruned quaternion weights that gives a comparable accuracy. The pruned quaternion network can be trained with only a small fraction of the parameters in the real GNN.

related_claims.content: Winning graph-lottery tickets exist for both real-valued GNNs and QMPNNs.

The MESSAGE, AGGREGATE, and UPDATE functions of any message-passing GNN are replaced by their quaternion counterparts so that the layerwise message-passing semantics are preserved in quaternion space.

Representing layer weights as quaternion matrices and grouping four real feature channels into one quaternion reduces the number of independent trainable real parameters by a factor of four relative to an equivalent real-valued GNN weight matrix.
the quaternion reparameterization is effective on large-scale graph benchmarks.

The parameter reduction described in claim 2 is achieved without increasing matrix-multiplication time complexity. [Referenced claim 2: Representing layer weights as quaternion matrices and grouping four real feature channels into one quaternion reduces the number of independent trainable real parameters by a factor of four relative to an equivalent real-valued GNN weight matrix.]

A quaternion weight mapping from $F$ real input features to $F'$ real outputs uses $F/4\times F'/4$ quaternion entries, yielding one-fourth the degrees of freedom of the corresponding real weight matrix.

When QMPNN variants of standard GNN architectures are trained under the same hyperparameters as those standard GNN architectures and evaluated on standard datasets, the quaternion models achieve comparable or better accuracy, ROC-AUC, or Hits@K (proportion of top-K predictions that are correct) while using roughly one-fourth of the trainable parameters of those standard GNN architectures.

When the three QMPNN variants QGCN, QGAT, and QSAGE of standard GNN architectures are trained under the same hyperparameters as those standard GNN architectures and evaluated on standard datasets, the quaternion models achieve comparable or better accuracy, ROC-AUC, or Hits@K (proportion of top-K predictions that are correct) while using roughly one-fourth of the trainable parameters of those standard GNN architectures.

Across all tasks and datasets evaluated, quaternion variants of standard GNN architectures frequently perform within a small margin of the corresponding real models and sometimes exceed their performance while consistently having approximately one-fourth the trainable parameter count of the corresponding real models.
QMPNN variants scale to large graph datasets and maintain performance comparable to real-valued GNNs while using fewer parameters.
Quaternion matrix multiplications have the same asymptotic time complexity as the corresponding real matrix multiplications.
